hints.title: Reverse Overwrite Invariant Obstacle
hints.text: Merging from the beginning of the first array overwrites unplaced elements unless an auxiliary buffer is used. Since the first array has trailing space reserved, from which direction can you place elements to avoid overwriting unmerged values?

hints.title: Backward Fill Invariant
hints.text: Compare the largest unplaced elements from both collections and place the larger value at the very end of the allocated buffer, working backward toward index zero.

hints.title: Three Pointer Backward Merge Procedure
hints.text: Set p1 to m minus one, p2 to n minus one, and write pointer p to m plus n minus one. While p2 is non-negative, compare elements: if p1 is valid and nums1[p1] is greater than nums2[p2], assign nums1[p1] to nums1[p] and decrement p1; otherwise assign nums2[p2] to nums1[p] and decrement p2. Decrement p at each step.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Reverse two-pointer merge directly into trailing buffer in O(1) space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Appending nums2 to nums1 and calling sort() takes O((M+N) log(M+N)) time, ignoring the sorted invariant of both arrays.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Forward merging requires an O(M) auxiliary array; backward merging requires O(1) extra space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Stopping the loop once p2 < 0 because remaining nums1 elements are already in their correct sorted positions.
